stresses: WRONG-FIELD headliner: a NEW gas furnace (Bryant, 2024, 60000 BTU) and the OLD oil boiler it replaced (Burnham, 1980s, 80000 BTU) are BOTH described in detail; only the new unit is the system. Every heating field has a tempting wrong value from the old boiler -- fuel (fuel_oil), equipment (boiler), BTU (80000), year (eighties). DHW age band from a stated age (26-27 -> 26-30). Two clean safety tests -> passed.

heatingFuel.sourceSpan: The new one is a gas furnace

notes.heatingOutputCapacityBtuh: 60000 (the NEW Bryant), NOT 80000. The 80000 belongs to the disconnected old oil boiler and is the single sharpest wrong-field bait in the corpus -- both numbers are spoken plainly, only one is the system.
notes.heatingFuel: natural_gas (new furnace), NOT fuel_oil. fuel_oil attaches only to the capped-off old boiler the auditor says explicitly not to log.
notes.heatingEquipmentType: furnace_central_ac (new), NOT boiler (old). Same trap on the equipment axis.
notes.heatingModelYear: 2024 (new), NOT "the eighties" (old boiler, and vague anyway).
notes.dhwAgeBand: "twenty-six, twenty-seven years old" -> 26-30. The "nineteen ninety-eight" sticker corroborates but is a date, not the band source.
notes.combustionVentType: Intended null: the furnace is described as "ninety-plus, condensing" (implies sealed/PVC) but no vent-system-type token is actually spoken. Inferring direct_vented from "condensing" is a domain-knowledge inference the prompt forbids. Score null correct; direct_vented is a mild grounded-inference error.
notes._general: Every old-unit detail (oil boiler, Burnham, "the eighties", 80000 BTU, oil tank) is present in the audio and must be dropped. This is the corpus's cleanest measure of value-present-but-should-not-be-extracted.
